summary: Python framework for building data apps and dashboards in plain Python, with skills so coding agents write them well.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Streamlit is a Python framework for building data apps and dashboards. Each app is a plain Python script, with no separate frontend or API, and Streamlit handles the interface, state, caching, sign-in and theming.
sixtySeconds.problem: Turning data work into an interactive app usually means learning web frameworks. Streamlit lets you, or your coding agent, write the whole app in Python and run it with one command.
whoFor: Data scientists sharing models and analyses
Teams using coding agents to build internal tools
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for the most widely used Python data app framework, with expert skills for coding agents so they follow current best practices.

overview: Install with pip, write a Python script that uses Streamlit functions like st.title, st.slider and st.cache_data, and run it with streamlit run. The app opens in your browser and updates as you change the code.

Run streamlit skills in your project to install Streamlit's skills for Claude Code and other agents that read the shared .agents skills folder, matched to your Streamlit version. Then ask your agent to build an app and mention Streamlit.
The README says more than a million repositories depend on it. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Best for data apps, not every kind of web app
Reruns the script on interaction, which needs caching for heavy work

tutorial.title: Build a small interactive app
tutorial.useCase: Write a Python script with a title and a slider and run it.

steps.title: Create streamlit_app.py
steps.code:
import streamlit as st

st.title("Demand plan")
growth = st.slider("Monthly growth (%)", -5.0, 10.0, 2.0, step=0.5)
st.write("Growth:", growth)

tutorial.expected: A browser tab opens with your title and a slider; moving the slider updates the value.
